claims.text: Hardware plan is a set of computing, storage and network resources the SP allocates as a target for tenant VM replicas
Comprises CPU and memory limits, storage quota (datastore/volume), number of networks
To tenants it appears as a cloud host usable as a regular target for replication and failover
Tenants see cloud hosts under VMware Cloud Hosts or Hyper-V Cloud Hosts nodes in Backup Infrastructure view
Hardware plans can be configured on VMware vSphere and Hyper-V, standalone hosts or clusters

A.notes: Omits that hardware plans are required to expose cloud hosts and that a tenant can subscribe to multiple plans on different hosts.

claims.text: Hardware plan is a set of resources the SP allocates to set up a target for tenant VM replicas
Cloud Connect provides one or more hardware plans whose resources are available to tenants as cloud hosts
Exposes computing, storage and network resources in SP environment as targets for tenant VM replicas
When subscribed, hardware plan appears in tenant infrastructure as a cloud host
Hardware plans exposed as cloud hosts on which tenants create VM replicas
Hardware plan has limits on CPU and RAM for all VM replicas on the cloud host
Configurable on a VMware host or cluster
Configurable on a Hyper-V host or cluster
VMware and Hyper-V hardware plan options in Replica Resources step of New Tenant wizard

B.notes: Omits that hardware plans are required to expose cloud hosts and multi-plan subscription across hosts.

claims.text: Maintenance window 'Allow backup server to prune old backups' lets you specify days to keep the backup
If agent creates no new restore points, backup remains for that period then is removed
Default retention for old backups is 30 days
Do not set to 1 day or similar short interval, the job may remove data you still require

A.notes: Omits that the Maintenance option is only available for Veeam backup repository / Cloud Connect repository destinations.

claims.text: --deleteold specifies days (1-999) to keep backup when no new restore points are created, then removed
Default retention policy keeps backup files for 7 days

B.notes: Gives the 7-day short-term retention default as if it were the stale-backup cleanup default; misses the 30-day Maintenance setting.
